A chromy sample as a survey design

Source: R/survey.R
as_svydesign.Rd

Hands the sample to the survey package: one row per selected unit, weighted by hits / expected_hits, so survey::svytotal() reproduces estimate_total()'s point estimates and the whole of survey's toolbox — ratios, regressions, domains, calibration — applies.

Usage

as_svydesign(x, ...)

Arguments

x

A chromy_sample().

...

Passed on to survey::svydesign().

Value

A survey.design object.

Details

The variance survey reports under this design (ids = ~1) is the with-replacement approximation: it ignores the implicit stratification the serpentine order bought, so it tends to be more conservative than the successive-difference variance of estimate_total(), which reads that order. Both are defensible reports; they answer slightly different questions about the same sample.

Examples

set.seed(7)
frame <- data.frame(size = rlnorm(80, 3), y = rlnorm(80, 5))
s <- chromy_sample(frame, n = 25, size = "size")
d <- as_svydesign(s)
survey::svytotal(~y, d)
#>   total     SE
#> y 23879 7603.4
estimate_total(s, "y")
#> # A tibble: 1 × 5
#>   variable  total    se cv_pct random_draws
#>   <chr>     <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>        <int>
#> 1 y        23879. 6865.   28.8           18
